cards.headline: White keeps two liberties after Black's retake, so Black must approach at A15 and White retakes for free: S[A-1KO-], not S[KO-].

diagrams.caption: The tree's line, marked S[KO-]. Black 9 took the ko, and White 12 retakes it, leaving Black 1, 3, 5 and 7 in atari at C17. Black to play.

diagrams.moves: A19! pass A15 B19 pass C17
diagrams.caption: One threat more than White, which S[KO-] says is enough. Black 13 retakes with it, and White 14 plays elsewhere, since White still has two liberties. Black 15 approaches, and White 16 retakes for free. Black has no threat left: Black 17 is elsewhere, and White 18 captures four stones and lives.

diagrams.moves: A19! pass A15 B19 A19! pass C17
diagrams.caption: If White 14 plays elsewhere, two threats more than White are enough: Black 17 retakes with the second, and Black 19 captures the ten White stones. This is the ko the label describes: one Black approach, Black 15, then a plain KO− with no local threats.

diagrams.moves: A19! F18 G19 B19 A19! pass A15 B19 A19! pass C17
diagrams.caption: White's best: White 14 uses the free move to atari Black 11 at F19 (the atari from G19 gives the same count). Black 15 is the best answer; capturing White 14 or ignoring it costs more. White 16 retakes for free. Black needs a third threat, for Black 21, before Black 23 captures; with two, Black has none left after White 20, and White captures at C17.

text: After White 12, Black must retake at A19 with a threat, but White's group keeps two liberties, A15 and C17. Neither side can fill C17: Black there lets White capture six stones at B19; White there lets Black capture the whole group at A15. So Black must approach at A15, and White retakes for free. One threat more than White, which is what S[KO-] means, is not enough (Diagram 2) in any search area the reviewers could decide.

White's capture needs no approach: if Black plays elsewhere instead of retaking, White captures at C17 even with four Black threats against none. After Black's approach the ko is a plain KO− (Diagram 3), so the leaf is an approach ko White took first: S[A-1KO-], as the solver said. White can also use the approach round's free move for an atari (Diagram 4), so Black needs three threats more in all. As in c121, which you set to S[A-1KO-], that gain belongs to the approach, not to the label.

Three threats win in every search area tried. That two fail is proven in the narrow areas, while some wider searches stay undecided; under your c121 rule this moves only the count, not the label. The label rests on reading that rule as covering this free move; if it covers only the free retake after the approach, the leaf is the strict S[A-1KO-2], still not S[KO-]. The first research's S[KO-3] had the right count, but in c121 you chose the approach form over KO-3 for this shape. No move's grade changes with any of these labels.

cards.headline: Question 8: the tree's S[KO-] is wrong either way: S[A-1KO-] with the right side closed, S[A-1KO-2] on the open board, where White's F18 atari is a local threat.

diagrams.caption: The tree's line to the leaf, marked S[KO-]. White 8 takes the ko by capturing Black 7, and Black 1, 3 and 5 are in atari at C17. Black to play.

diagrams.moves: A19! pass A17 A16 F19 A18 A17! pass A18 C17 A15
diagrams.caption: With the right side closed. Black 9 retakes after a ko threat elsewhere but threatens nothing yet, so White 10 plays elsewhere. Black 11 captures White 2 and forces White 12, Black 13 approaches, and White 14 captures Black 11 for free, a second ko. Black 15 retakes after a second threat. White's atari at a would be no threat, so Black 17 kills; Black 19 captures when White 18 fills a liberty. With only one threat more than White, Black has none for Black 15, and White lives by capturing at B19.

The open board. White 16 ataris Black 13, and Black 17 must answer; here it captures White 16. White 18 retakes the second ko for free, so Black needs a third threat. Answering at G19 instead is no better.

The open board, if Black 17 ignores the atari and connects. White 18 takes Black 13, and White's group has three liberties to Black's two. Black 19 fills one, but White 20 and White 22 get out, and every Black move then loses; Black's other tries fail too, a few by reading only. In the solver's narrow area, even with G19 and H19 added, the right side is closed: White's stones die against the wall, and Black 19 wins.

text: White 8's capture threatens at once: if Black plays elsewhere, White captures three stones at C17 and lives. Black must retake, but the retake threatens nothing yet, so Black needs one approach, Black 13 in Diagram 2, and White 14 then captures in a second ko for free. With one threat more than White, Black fails wherever the search decided it, and opening the board only helps White: S[KO-] is wrong under either answer. The fight then switches through the second ko: your 10403 shape, which you rated a one-move approach ko for Black.

The two answers differ on White 16 in Diagrams 3 and 4, an atari on Black 13 after the approach. With the right side closed, as in the solver's narrow area, Black can ignore it, since White's stones die against the wall: after the approach Black needs one threat more than White, and the leaf is S[A-1KO-] (Diagram 2). On the open board Black must answer (Diagram 4) and White retakes for free (Diagram 3): Black needs two threats more after the approach, S[A-1KO-2].

At k024 in this tree, the same atari works only in the approach round, where your c121 rule keeps it out of the label; here it also works after the approach. Whether White's free move in this leaf's approach round gains a threat as well is undecided; the rule would keep that out. The open-board lines ran in areas still more favourable to Black, so White's wins there carry over; that one approach suffices on the open board rests on reading, as do Black's other approaches and a few side lines. No move's grade changes under either answer.
